recent_posts.title: How to use Ubuntu on Windows
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to running Ubuntu on Windows using four approaches: Hyper-V, VirtualBox, Multipass, and WSL2. Covers how each virtualization method works, their trade-offs (GPU support, performance, isolation), and how to automate setup with cloud-init. Also details enterprise management using Ubuntu Pro for WSL, Microsoft Intune, Canonical Landscape, and Entra ID integration for compliance, auditing, and privilege tracking in regulated environments.

recent_posts.title: Fixes available for CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail) Linux Kernel Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
recent_posts.summary: A high-severity (CVSS 7.8) local privilege escalation vulnerability, CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail), has been disclosed in the Linux kernel's algif_aead module, which provides hardware-accelerated cryptographic functions. All Ubuntu releases before Resolute (26.04) are affected. The Ubuntu Security Team has released mitigations via the kmod package that disable the vulnerable module. A full kernel patch is also forthcoming. The post details how to check if your system is impacted, how to apply the kmod mitigation or manually block the module, and how to handle edge cases like running containers or applications that may not gracefully fall back to software cryptography.

recent_posts.title: Run NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni locally in a single command
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA has launched Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, an open multimodal foundation model supporting text, images, video, audio, and documents with a 256K token context window and hybrid MoE architecture. Canonical is making it instantly deployable on Ubuntu via a single snap command (`sudo snap install nemotron-3-nano-omni`). Inference snaps bundle the model, runtime, and dependencies into a single portable artifact, enabling zero-friction deployment across edge, workstation, cloud, and on-premises environments without manual configuration or dependency management.

recent_posts.title: What makes web engineering worth working in
recent_posts.summary: A senior web engineering manager at Canonical reflects on what makes web development compelling: its broad accessibility across devices, the quality and DevOps discipline required to keep web apps running reliably, the ongoing innovation between core web technologies (HTML, CSS, JS) and frameworks, and the richness of the full web stack. The post also touches on emerging technologies like Web Components and WebGPU, and closes with a brief overview of Canonical's web team structure and a recruitment pitch.

recent_posts.title: Ubuntu 16.04 LTS has reached the end of standard Expanded Security Maintenance with Ubuntu Pro. Here are your options.
recent_posts.summary: Ubuntu 16.04 LTS (Xenial Xerus) has reached the end of its five-year Expanded Security Maintenance (ESM) window in April 2026. Organizations still running 16.04 have two options: upgrade progressively to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, or activate the Legacy add-on for Ubuntu Pro, which extends security maintenance for an additional five years (until April 2031). The Legacy add-on covers security patches for the Linux kernel, critical packages like MySQL 5.7, Python 2.7, PostgreSQL 9.5, and NGINX 1.10, plus OpenStack Mitaka support. It is aimed at organizations with complex hardware, proprietary stacks, or regulatory requirements that prevent immediate migration.

recent_posts.title: Understanding disaggregated GenAI model serving with llm-d
recent_posts.summary: llm-d is an open source, cloud-native system for high-scale LLM deployments that addresses latency and memory-bandwidth bottlenecks by disaggregating the inference workload across dedicated hardware. It splits processing into four Kubernetes-managed components: an inference scheduler (adaptive load balancer using Prometheus metrics), a KV cache manager, a prefill worker for compute-intensive prompt processing, and a decode worker for token generation. The post explains why organizations with data sovereignty requirements would self-host LLMs, highlights the availability of competitive open-weight models, and shares experimental Juju charms the author built to simplify llm-d deployments on Ubuntu without requiring deep Kubernetes expertise.

recent_posts.title: Canonical releases Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Resolute Raccoon
recent_posts.summary: Canonical has released Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon', the 11th long-term supported Ubuntu release. Key highlights include: Linux 7.0 kernel with Intel Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) support; native NVIDIA CUDA and AMD ROCm distribution via official repositories for AI/ML workloads; Rust-based system utilities (sudo-rs, uutils coreutils) and Rust kernel drivers for memory safety; TPM-backed full-disk encryption now generally available; Canonical Livepatch extended to Arm64 servers for rebootless kernel patching; full Wayland adoption completing the X.org transition; GNOME desktop with improved accessibility; confidential computing support for Intel TDX and AMD SEV; RISC-V RVA23 baseline support; and Authd for cloud identity provider authentication (Entra ID, Google IAM, OIDC).

recent_posts.title: From Jammy to Resolute: how Ubuntu’s toolchains have evolved
recent_posts.summary: Ubuntu's toolchain evolution from 22.04 LTS (Jammy) to 26.04 LTS (Resolute Raccoon) is reviewed, highlighting the shift from basic compiler availability to a curated, framework-aware development platform. Key additions include devpacks for Spring and Go that bundle framework tools into single-command installs, an official .NET snap with multi-version management, OpenJDK 25 with memory and startup improvements, Rust 1.93 with cargo-auditable support, and Golang 1.26 as default. The strategy aims to reduce developer onboarding from multi-page setup guides to a few commands, with future plans for C/C++ dev stacks, Python framework devpacks, and deeper rustup integration.

recent_posts.title: Hybrid search and reranking: a deeper look at RAG
recent_posts.summary: Production-grade RAG systems require more than basic vector search. Hybrid search combines dense vector search (semantic similarity) with sparse full-text search (BM25) to improve recall, merging results using algorithms like Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) or weighted average scoring. A reranking model (cross-encoder) then takes the top 50–100 hybrid search candidates and re-scores them by evaluating the query and document together, surfacing the most relevant 5–10 chunks for the LLM. The post includes a PostgreSQL SQL example implementing hybrid search with RRF using pgvector and tsvector, and explains where each stage (embeddings, hybrid search, reranking) belongs in the architecture stack.

recent_posts.title: Canonical expands Ubuntu support to next-generation MediaTek Genio 520 and 720 platforms
recent_posts.summary: Canonical has announced early access Ubuntu 24.04 LTS images for MediaTek's new Genio 520 and 720 IoT platforms, expanding an existing partnership that already covers Genio 350, 510, 700, and 1200. The Genio 520 targets power-efficient IoT applications like smart home hubs and industrial gateways, while the Genio 720 focuses on advanced multimedia and on-device AI workloads including robotics and medical imaging. The release aims to accelerate time-to-market for edge AI deployments, offering enterprise-grade security, 15-year LTS support, and a path toward EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) compliance. Images are publicly available for download and flashing on MediaTek Genio development kits.
